segments.narration: Divers found seventy ancient ships stacked in one bay. Abu Qir, east of Alexandria, seven kilometres offshore and six metres down.
This was Thonis-Heracleion, Egypt's gateway for foreign trade for centuries before Alexandria existed. Temples, gold coins, a statue holding four loaves of bread.
A granite slab carried a decree of Nectanebo the First and the city's real Egyptian name. So how does an entire port disappear?
The ground gave way. Around 101 BC heavy flooding liquefied the clay under the central island, and earthquakes and rising sea finished the job.
Franck Goddio's team located the city in 2000, after five years of searching the bay. He reckons about five percent has been excavated.
